stories.title: AI jobs boom is leaving women behind in top-paying roles
stories.simple_summary: New AI jobs are being created, but women are not getting many of the highest-paying positions in this field.
stories.why_it_matters: If you're hiring for tech roles or planning your career, you should know that AI job opportunities are growing but may not be equally available to everyone.

stories.title: OpenAI hit the brakes. Now what?
stories.simple_summary: OpenAI, a major AI company, decided to slow down and take a two-week pause on some of its AI work to focus on making things safer and more secure instead of rushing ahead.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors and tech industry people — nothing you need to act on right now.

stories.title: Stripe Agrees to Buy AI Firm OpenRouter; No Terms Disclosed
stories.simple_summary: Stripe, a payment company, bought an AI company called OpenRouter. The price wasn't announced.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors — nothing you need to act on.

stories.title: Meta AI is getting a Mac app
stories.simple_summary: Meta made a new app for Apple computers that lets you share what's on your screen with their AI assistant, which can answer questions and help create things.
stories.why_it_matters: If you use a Mac and already use Meta's AI, you now have easier access to it on your computer.

stories.title: The A.I. in Google’s New Pixel 11 Is Not Very Helpful
stories.simple_summary: Google's new Pixel 11 phone has AI features built in, but they don't seem to be very useful yet.
stories.why_it_matters: If you're thinking about buying a new Android phone, the AI features may not yet be worth paying extra for.

stories.title: TerraPower’s nuclear reactor has a secret weapon for powering AI data centers
stories.simple_summary: A company called TerraPower is building a nuclear power plant that could be a good fit for powering the huge computers that AI companies need.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors and data center companies — nothing you need to act on.

stories.title: Marvell pops 6% on AI chip deal that lets Google buy up to $12.2 billion in shares
stories.simple_summary: Google agreed to buy computer chips from Marvell, a chip maker, and the deal could be worth up to $12.2 billion, which made Marvell's stock price jump.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors — nothing you need to act on.

stories.title: Amazon makes its AI-powered Alexa+ free on Fire TV, no Prime required
stories.simple_summary: Amazon is making its upgraded Alexa AI assistant free on Fire TV devices for everyone, even people who don't pay for Prime membership.
stories.why_it_matters: If you own a Fire TV device, you may get access to a better AI assistant at no extra cost.

stories.title: Calendly throws its hat into meeting note-taker circus
stories.simple_summary: Calendly, the meeting scheduling website, is adding an AI assistant called Callie that helps take notes during meetings.
stories.why_it_matters: If your small business uses Calendly to schedule meetings, you may soon have an AI tool to help keep track of what was discussed.

stories.title: How the use of artificial intelligence harms college students’ ability to learn
stories.simple_summary: Research shows that when students use AI to do their work, it can hurt their ability to actually learn the material.
stories.why_it_matters: If you have kids or grandkids in school, this is worth knowing — relying on AI instead of doing the work yourself makes learning harder.

stories.title: AI isn’t close to curing cancer. This startup says it knows what it will take.
stories.simple_summary: A startup says that using AI to help cure cancer is hard because the real problem is having enough good data to work with.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to medical researchers and investors — nothing you need to act on.

stories.title: Nvidia’s new financial strategy does not compute
stories.simple_summary: Major finance companies are working with Nvidia (a chip maker) to create a $500 billion funding plan that treats computer power as a tradeable product, similar to how stocks or bonds work.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors and financial professionals — nothing you need to act on.
